name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Kugayama-san and buddy. This is the moment of truth."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It's quite a long story. Would that be alright?"

name: Shiori
message: "Yes... but, um, just one thing first."

name: Shiori
message: "It feels rather odd talking with you outside the library like this."

name: Shiori
message: "I mean, you're a librarian. Besides, didn't you say you couldn't leave the library?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Ah, you weren't there when it happened. Then let me start by explaining this morning's events."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Come sit down so we can talk."
(Sit on the bench)

name: Shiori
message: "Something that important had to happen today, of all days..."

name: Shiori
message: "I kind of wish I'd seen your reaction back then."

name: Shiori
message: "No, that'd be unfair of me. It's my fault for disappearing without saying anything."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Let's leave it at that and move on to the main issue."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Please take out your phone."
(Take out your smartphone)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I've continued investigating the case since I last spoke with you two."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "After realizing the limits of analog sources, I decided to rely on a computer."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Repeated freezes. Endless reboots. After overcoming countless trials and diving deep into the sea of the internet, I finally arrived at a certain suspicion."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It was about the true identity of Man Y, posted on a so-called underground message board."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It claimed that Man Y might be Councilor Yasuda's son."

name: Shiori
message: "Councilor Yasuda?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "A politician whose support base is this town, Hikarigadai."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And the one Tetsuya-san was pursuing."

name: Shiori
message: "Then the one who shut down Tetsuya-san's article was this Councilor Yasuda person?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It's extremely likely. Even if it wasn't him personally, I'm almost certain someone under his influence did it."

name: Shiori
message: "And the person we spoke to yesterday was his son?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Most likely."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The internet was overflowing with negative rumors about them."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Allegations concerning money, the fact that his son was appointed as a public secretary despite not actually working, and so on."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It seems the times have changed."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "We no longer live in a world where a single individual can control the flow of information."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Not Yasuda, not anyone."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That said, information has also become a mixed bag."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The suspicion that 'Man Y' is Councilor Yasuda's son is likely just a form of envy."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "There is no evidence whatsoever. In short, it is unreliable information that ought to be ignored—under normal circumstances, at least."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You've probably already figured it out. The next step would be to investigate Councilor Yasuda's son."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You've seen the face of the ghost you believe to be the culprit. In other words, you should be capable of judging whether or not he is the same person."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Now search for 'Councilor Yasuda, public secretary, son.' Run an image search. A photo of his face should come up."
(Councilor Yasuda, public secretary, son.)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "...There it is."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The one on the left is Councilor Yasuda. On the right is his son, Takeyuki."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Well? Do you recognize this face?"

name: Shiori
message: "What do you think? I already know what my answer is."
"Yes."
"I think."

name: Shiori
message: "Yes, I agree. There's no doubt about it. This is the man I was waiting to show up."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Very good. Now we know who the man in the park was."

name: Shiori
message: "I see. So that's your take on it."

name: Shiori
message: "But I remember him clearly."

name: Shiori
message: "Because, you see, I've been thinking about yesterday all night long."

name: Shiori
message: "So I'm sure of it. It's him."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Then the ghost at the park was Councilor Yasuda's son, Yasuda Takeyuki. From here on, I'll refer to him as Yasuda."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Yasuda claims he was killed by Kugayama-san, and that information led you into that state. Is that correct, Kugayama-san?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "While this is only a general tendency, and I can't really say for certain..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Ghosts with hazy memories can sometimes link different ones together and mix them up."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "He knows Kugayama-san. And he believes he was killed by someone. It is entirely possible that he confused those two memories, leading him to believe that Kugayama-san was the one who killed him."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It happens quite often. Ghosts tend to create false memories."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "On the other hand, if he truly does have a clear, reliable memory, then the credibility of his testimony becomes questionable in a different way."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Yasuda and his father, Councilor Yasuda, are people who have plastered everything in lies."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Their delusions aren't worth listening to."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You don't need to take his words to heart. His testimony is already dubious as it is."

name: Shiori
message: "Thank you. I feel a little bit better now."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It's still too soon to thank me."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I've only just laid out two hypotheses side by side."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "We can still take our inference one step further."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The following keywords should lead us to the answer already: 'Councilor Yasuda, son, suicide.'"
(Councilor Yasuda, son, suicide)

name: Shiori
message: "Suicide...?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "There it is. The top article should do. Please open it."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It's news about a councilor's son's death. The article clearly states it was a suicide."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And that's exactly what it was. Yasuda took his own life. In short, you didn't kill him, Kugayama-san."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That said, since he knew you, there's no doubt the two of you had some kind of connection while he was alive."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And although he denies committing any crime, the fact that he accused you of killing your own sister means he knows something about the case."

name: Shiori
message: "At this point, it's probably safe to say that Man Y was Yasuda."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Yes, I agree."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "'I was killed by Kugayama-san.' 'Kugayama-san killed her own sister.' Those statements are likely the result of confused memories."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "As for why coverage of the case suddenly stopped, it's because the suspect, Yasuda, had already died..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Plus his father, Councilor Yasuda, may have stepped in."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Just like when Tetsuya-san's article was shot down."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I'm well aware that this is only speculation, colored by my own biases."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Which is why I want to help you two as well."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I want to make the truth clear."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "On the surface, the only outlet pursuing Yasuda was the magazine that was eventually shut down."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "But it's likely that other magazines, newspapers, and television networks were also investigating Yasuda behind the scenes."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The police must've been pursuing him as well. Hounded by both the police and the media, Yasuda chose to take his own life."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Councilor Yasuda wanted to cover up his son's crimes. The police and the media also didn't want it made public that they drove a suspect to his death."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Their interests aligned, and the coverage suddenly stopped."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "If you think about it that way, it all falls into place, don't you agree?"

name: Shiori
message: "I suppose so... At the very least, it doesn't seem completely off the mark."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Inexplicable things tend to happen around so-called members of the elite."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It's something I realized after looking into various materials as part of Tetsuya-san's investigation."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Given that these strange things are actually occurring, we can't simply dismiss them as nonsensical."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That said, the reason Yasuda took his own life is beside the point."

name: Shiori
message: "Huh? Why?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "What matters most to us right now is the nature of his relationship with Kugayama-san."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "If we let ourselves get caught up in trivial matters, we'll lose sight of our goal."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "We should make our objective clear."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Our first priority is to restore Kugayama-san's memories and ensure they don't slip away."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And to do that, we need to uncover the truth behind this case."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Since Yasuda's testimony lacks credibility, we have no choice but to look for the other key figure: Girl A."

name: Shiori
message: "Okay. But where do we even start? What are we supposed to look into now, and how?"

name: Shiori
message: "After all, we can't trust what Yasuda said, right?"

name: Shiori
message: "And I don't think we can figure everything out just from what we find on the internet..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I have a proposal."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It is as you say. There are limits to what we can learn from the internet, newspapers, or magazines."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And it wouldn't be realistic to go around asking random people. It would help if we had a specialist, but we don't have those kinds of connections."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That's why, I suggest we rely on our 'ties.'"

name: Shiori
message: "Ties?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "In life, I was a logical and rational person. I wasn't the type who believed in anything unscientific. But that's no longer the case."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Even my very existence is unscientific now. Since becoming a ghost, I've come to place importance on spiritual approaches to thinking and belief."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "This is no more than a hypothesis I've drawn from my own experience, so before I begin, I should clarify that it lacks solid grounding."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "What are the conditions under which people can perceive ghosts, which should normally be invisible?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I believe it boils down to whether the two are 'tied' to one another, whether they are beings that influence each other. Put simply, whether there is a 'tie' between them."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Tetsuya-san can't see me as he is now. Because for the time being, we each have our own different roles to fulfill. Or so I believe."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "As someone who is already dead, I can't involve myself too deeply in Tetsuya-san's life, which will still stretch far into the future."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And so, after I fulfilled my role, I was removed from Tetsuya-san's life. Our tie was severed."

name: Shiori
message: "But that's too..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It's all right. I'm not being sentimental. This is just how things are meant to be."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Everything boils down to ties. There are likely countless ghosts in this world, but only those bound by them can be seen."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The reason our buddy can still see me is because a tie remains. Unlike with Tetsuya-san, we can even speak to each other."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "In truth, you bore a role that was too great for me."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I became so fixated on my promise with Tetsuya-san—that we'd see each other tomorrow. And before I knew it, I was bound to the library."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "But then you two stepped in and put an end to it."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Because of you two, I am free once more."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "My tie with both of you sent my time back into motion."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "But our buddy here can still see me, hear me."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Which means my role is not yet finished."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Until I repay my debt to you two, this tie will remain."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "In short, every encounter you've had up to now has had a meaning."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Whether it was you or Kugayama-san, people and ghosts meet because they share a tie and have roles to fulfill."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The ghosts tied to the two of you may be able to guide us to the answer."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "First, let us sort through the ghosts you've encountered so far, one by one."
(Shiori-san)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Most likely, the ghost with the strongest tie to you would be Kugayama-san."

name: Shiori
message: "Yes, I agree."

name: Shiori
message: "It's like there's this special feeling that only pops up when I'm with you."

name: Shiori
message: "I think that's what she means by our tie being strong."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Your role here might be to recover Kugayama-san's memories."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And perhaps it is mine as well. If it weren't for Kugayama-san, I probably would never have met you."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Now is the time for the three of us to work together. The answer should already be in reach."

name: Shiori
message: "Indeed."
(Ms. Librarian)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You already know my real name, but let's leave things as they are. It would feel strange to be called by name now."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I'm sorry to say that I had no involvement in the Preschool Girl Serial Kidnapping and Murder Case. The same goes for Tetsuya-san as well."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I know nothing about the case itself. But while I can't provide information, I'm useful in other ways."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Even after becoming a ghost, many still come to me for advice."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "After all, there is no one more knowledgeable about ghosts than me."

name: Shiori
message: "I think I understand how those ghosts must've felt."

name: Shiori
message: "Talking with you just feels reassuring, somehow."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "So please continue making good use of me, an intellectual and experienced ghost."
(Gyaruko-san)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I suppose I owe her as well."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "If she hadn't introduced me to you two, I never would have seen Tetsuya-san again."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Her real name is Kirishiki Nagisa, is it? And she regained her memories one step ahead of Kugayama-san."

name: Shiori
message: "Yes. I still remember when I mentioned her name."

name: Shiori
message: "Apparently, her memories went whoooooosh, and it all came flooding back."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The sensation of regaining one's memories differs from person to person."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She must be the intuitive type, then. By the way, what was the cause of her death?"

name: Shiori
message: "She said she fell from her apartment building, on her own, apparently."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "An accidental fall... Could you show me the related articles?"
(Take out your smartphone)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "...I see. The fall occurred before the Serial Kidnapping and Murder Case."

name: Shiori
message: "In other words, Gyaruko-san can't be Girl A."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Even so, she is unquestionably a key person."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And Kirishiki-san was the one who told you that Yasuda, the most likely suspect, would appear at the playground."

name: Shiori
message: "Yes, Gyaruko-san was the one who told us."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Starting with Kirishiki-san, the two of you formed ties one by one."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It might be worth hearing her out again. Perhaps a new encounter will turn the situation around."
(The man at the park)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Indeed, one could say that the two of you have ties with Yasuda."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "But as I warned you earlier, confronting Yasuda should come last."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It would be dangerous to take his testimony at face value."
(Kashima Reiko-san)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "A woman well-versed in urban legends... is it?"

name: Shiori
message: "She might've been joking, but she kept saying things like she'd committed countless sins."

name: Shiori
message: "But, um, yes... she must've been. I'm sure of it."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She's a young woman... in short, a possible candidate for Girl A, though she doesn't seem like a bad person. Would that be correct?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I suggest we determine exactly when she died. If we can rule her out as a candidate, that alone would be a major step forward."

name: Shiori
message: "Yes. Suspecting someone you know can get exhausting, after all."
(The gossiping woman)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "A woman who's in the know. She tends to embellish, so her credibility is somewhat questionable. Is that correct?"

name: Shiori
message: "I'm... not really good with her..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That said, at the very least, everything we've heard from her so far, while exaggerated, hasn't been a lie."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "In short, she is a valuable source of information, so I'd like to hear what she has to say about the case as well, but..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It might be better to leave that for later."

name: Shiori
message: "Huh? Oh, um, it's true I'm not good with her, but you don't need to worry about me."

name: Shiori
message: "I want to face the truth too."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Of course. That wasn't why I suggested it."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You mentioned that she tends to embellish her stories."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Given how limited our own information is, it will be difficult to tell how much of it is embellishment."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "But with enough information, we can judge which parts are exaggerations or misunderstandings."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "We should go see her once the time is right."
(Uribayashi, Rina)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "A woman pushing a stroller with a doll in it... is that so?"

name: Shiori
message: "She isn't a ghost, but she was apparently involved in a child abduction incident in the past."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "We don't know when that abduction occurred, but if it was around the same time as the Serial Kidnapping and Murder Case, she would become a strong candidate for Girl A."
(Micchan's mother)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "A woman pushing a stroller with a doll in it. She's not a ghost, but she may be a person of interest. Is that correct?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And someone you happened to run into by chance. So while she seems unrelated to the case..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The fact that she could see Kugayama-san means there must be some kind of tie."

name: Shiori
message: "If your theory is correct, then she must have a role to play as well."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "However, she can't hear ghosts, and her mental state is questionable, so it's unclear whether she can even hold a proper conversation with you, buddy."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I can't say whether we'll be able to obtain any useful information from her, but for now, we should still keep her in mind."
(The fleeting woman)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "A young woman you saw at the flower garden..."

name: Shiori
message: "She didn't react at all when I spoke to her. She was in no state to communicate."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "From what you're telling me... she's in the final stages. In my experience, ghosts on the verge of fading tend to show symptoms like that."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That said, it may simply be a natural step on the path to passing on. Someone like me, who clings to this world indefinitely, is probably the unnatural one."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "But what is truly right or wrong, only God knows. It would probably be best to simply leave her alone."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "...Or at least, that's what I would normally say."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "But even this encounter may have some meaning as well."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Of course, it's very possible that it's unrelated to Kugayama-san, but it may still be worth going to see her."
(The little ghost girl)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The ghost you two have been searching for, who may be a victim of the case—"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "—and the ghost Kugayama-san believes might be her younger sister."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Furthermore, that ghost rejected Kugayama-san, which only caused her further distress. Is that correct?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I'd like to meet her as well. I'm curious about the sense of unease our buddy mentioned."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That should bring our situation into order."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Now, it's finally time to get moving."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "If we can clarify Kugayama-san's relationship with Yasuda, that alone may be enough to prove her innocence... perhaps."

name: Shiori
message: "Ms. Librarian? Is something wrong? Weren't we going to speak with the ghosts tied to us?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Now that I've noticed, I suppose I should tell you."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "We're being followed."

name: Shiori
message: "Followed?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "There's someone tailing us. Look, her."

name: Shiori
message: "Huh, ah—She's here!"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I've sensed her presence for quite awhile now. She has probably been following us since we found you at the playground... or perhaps even earlier."

name: Shiori
message: "Wait, since way back then?! I didn't notice at all..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Shall we hear what she has to say first?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She's been watching us for a while now... or more precisely, our buddy, the entire time."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She must be the little ghost girl you mentioned earlier, yes?"
"Yes."
(Nod)

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Fortune seems to be on our side. I didn't think we'd meet her so soon."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Let's speak to her."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You are... unexpectedly mischievous... We're already outside the library, yet you deliberately answered with a silent nod."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Well, no matter. I'll take it as a sign that we've grown close enough for little pranks."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Good thing I'm a rational ghost with a sense of humor."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Now then, let's pull ourselves together and speak to her."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Hold on for a moment, both of you."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I see. I've figured out the source of the unease you felt."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "This girl... isn't a ghost."
"She's alive?"
"She's a yokai?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "No, rather... How should I explain this..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You're perceptive. Yes, she's something close to that."

name: Shiori
message: "What do you mean? Are yokai different from ghosts?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Are you familiar with urban legends? Hanako-san of the Toilet, the Kuchisake-onna, Mary-san. They're quite famous, but perhaps younger people these days don't know them?"
"I've met some of them."
"I know them."
"I don't know them."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Is that so? That's quite a rare and valuable experience you've had, then..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You're well-informed. That makes things easier."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I... see. I can really feel the generational gap."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Urban legends are born from rumors that people spread. This girl is something close to that."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Not a human soul, but something formed from human thoughts."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "This is only conjecture, but she may have been born from the regrets of the victims and their families."

name: Shiori
message: "The regrets... of their families..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I found an article about a group led by the victims' families. They were campaigning for the disclosure of the investigation's progress."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Even after five years, the families haven't given up on seeing the case solved. And that's only natural. Their precious daughters were taken from them."

name: Shiori
message: "The perpetrator was never caught, and media coverage suddenly ceased. The case remains unsolved. There's no way for them to find closure."

name: Shiori
message: "I... think I understand how they feel... their regrets..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Five years' worth of regrets, piling up without relief, taking on the victims' forms and wandering the town."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I've seen something similar before. The sensation is unique to ghosts, so it's difficult to put into words..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Perhaps it's akin to the sense of unease our buddy is feeling, something different from what one feels when facing a ghost."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "That said, the idea of her being tied to the victims is merely speculation, or rather, almost pure conjecture. Still, there is some basis for it."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Kugayama-san, when you approached her and spoke to her, she cried out in rejection, yes?"

name: Shiori
message: "Yes."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "There's something I'd like to try. Could you try approaching her instead?"
(Approach the girl)
The girl stares intently at you.

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Thank you. Now, I will try approaching her."

name: Shiori
message: "She ran away... Why?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Just as I expected. It seems she was wary of me and Kugayama-san, which is why she kept her distance. It wasn't hard to guess how she'd react if I approached her."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Kugayama-san, it seems she isn't rejecting you specifically, but adult women in general."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You may be a student, but from her perspective, you must still fall within the category of an adult."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "In short, she isn't your sister nor is she rejecting anyone specifically. She's hostile only toward adult women."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Most likely, because of Girl A."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "The lingering thoughts left behind by the victims probably still hold the memory of being abducted by Girl A."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Therefore, it's reasonable to think that fear manifested as rejection."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Unfortunately, this alone isn't enough to rule you out as an accomplice. But it's almost certain that she isn't your sister."

name: Shiori
message: "So she wasn't my sister..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "...She came back."

name: Shiori
message: "Huh? You're right."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It looks like she's taken an interest in our buddy. In other words, the one she's tied to might not be you, but our friend here."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "As for what to call her... yes, let us refer to her as a thought-form."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Like with ghosts, it may be possible to communicate with her."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Shall we try? As long as I don't approach her, she shouldn't run away."
(Approach the girl)
"Hello."
(Do a threatening anteater pose)
The girl hides behind a tree in the distance.

name: Shiori
message: "She ran away."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "But her reaction is completely different from when it was me. At the very least, she isn't rejecting you."
The girl hides behind a tree in the distance.

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "...What exactly are you doing? You suddenly struck a bizarre pose out of nowhere. People will think you're strange."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "...Please be a bit more mindful of how others see you. At least for your own sake."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It's no wonder the girl ran away. That said... at the very least, she wasn't rejecting you."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She really does have a clear interest in our buddy. I'm curious as to why, but..."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "For now, shall we leave the park?"

name: Shiori
message: "She's following us."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "She shouldn't approach as long as Kugayama-san and I stay close to you. As long as we don't get too complacent, it should be fine."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Now, let us begin the investigation."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Shall we start by questioning the ghosts tied to us?"
